issues.title: Sparse Select for BitPacking segments (decode only selected rows)
issues.hypothesis: In q02 the partsupp probe scan is the largest single cost: 0.30s CPU summed over threads (about 37ms per thread at 8 threads, out of 71ms total). I measured its parts in isolation, hot: a plain 8M-row ps_partkey scan costs 0.02s; ps_partkey with the BF filter costs 0.08s (the BF hash+probe is about 7ns/row, already tight in bloom_filter.cpp); adding the two payload columns ps_suppkey and ps_supplycost raises it to 0.30s. Only about 1% of rows survive the BF (73k of 8M, about 18 rows per 2048-row vector), yet the payload columns cost about as much as a full 3-column scan (0.14s). The cause is in StandardColumnData::Select (src/storage/table/standard_column_data.cpp:103). It uses a specialised segment select only when the compression function has `select`. Only dict_fsst and constant implement it. BitPacking (src/storage/compression/bitpacking.cpp, GetBitpackingFunction) does not, so ColumnData::Select falls back to Scan (decode all 2048 values) plus Slice. Both payload columns are BitPacking with Constant validity, and Constant validity already has ConstantSelectValidity. So adding a bitpacking select is the only missing piece for the fast path.
issues.plan: In src/storage/compression/bitpacking.cpp add template<class T> BitpackingSelect(ColumnSegment&, ColumnScanState&, idx_t vector_count, Vector &result, const SelectionVector &sel, idx_t sel_count), modelled on FSSTStorage::Select (fsst.cpp:713). It writes result_data[i] = value at row sel.get_index(i) for i < sel_count (flat result). It must leave the BitpackingScanState advanced by exactly vector_count rows, as a scan would. (1) Dense case (sel_count * 4 > vector_count), or the current metadata group is DELTA_FOR: decode the vector with BitpackingScanPartial<T> into a scratch buffer of STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE T held lazily in the scan state, then gather through sel. This costs the same as today, so it cannot regress. (2) Sparse case: walk the selected indices in ascending order (sel is ascending in scans) and keep a cursor `pos`. For each idx call scan_state.Skip(segment, idx - pos). Skip is O(1) for CONSTANT, CONSTANT_DELTA and FOR, crossing metadata groups by pointer arithmetic. Then read the single value the way BitpackingFetchRow does. Handle the case current_group_offset == BITPACKING_METADATA_GROUP_SIZE by calling LoadNextGroup first, as BitpackingScanPartial does. Cache the last unpacked 32-value algorithm group pointer so that neighbouring rows are not unpacked twice. For a DELTA_FOR group, Skip decodes and keeps current_delta_offset, so it stays correct, just not faster; the value is decoded the same way Skip's loop does. At the end call Skip(vector_count - pos). Register it in GetBitpackingFunction by setting `bitpacking.select = BitpackingSelect<T>;`, the same way dict_fsst.cpp:294 sets `res.select`. Check that the select function pointer signature matches compression_function.hpp. Run the bitpacking tests under test/sql/storage/compression/bitpacking/, plus selective-filter queries on persisted tables.
issues.expected_gain: q02: payload-column cost in the partsupp scan drops from about 0.22s to about 0.03s CPU, so the scan goes from 0.30s to about 0.11s. That is roughly 15-25% of q02 wall time, because this scan is the critical path of the probe pipeline.
issues.generality: Any persisted-table scan where a pushed filter (constant comparison, bloom-filter/IN join filter, LIKE) keeps a small fraction of each vector and the projected columns are bitpacked integers, decimals or dates. That is very common: selective joins into fact tables, TPC-H/TPC-DS-style payload columns. Dense selections use the old decode-then-gather path, so the only possible slowdown is the extra branch per vector.
issues.risk: Medium-low. The bitpacking scan state must end up exactly where a full Scan would have left it, including metadata-group crossing and DELTA_FOR's current_delta_offset. A mistake gives wrong values for later vectors, but the bitpacking test suite and the hidden result checks should catch that. Falling back for DELTA_FOR and dense selections keeps the new code to the simple random-access modes.

issues.hypothesis: Carried over from the backlog. The supplier scan emits 96k rows where about 20k match s_nationkey IN (5 keys), because PushInFilter makes a zonemap-only OptionalFilter. In isolation the hot 7-column supplier scan costs 0.05s CPU at 8 threads against 0.01s at 1 thread. Scanning only 20% of the string columns through Select (FSST has select) would cut its cost.
issues.plan: In JoinFilterPushdownInfo::PushInFilter (src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp), for an integral key and an IN list of 8 values or fewer on an inner or semi join, wrap the IN filter in a SelectivityOptionalFilter (src/planner/filter/selectivity_optional_filter.cpp) instead of a plain OptionalFilter, so it runs on rows and switches itself off when it is not selective. Note that RowGroup::CheckZonemap (row_group.cpp:626) marks every filter of type OPTIONAL_FILTER as always-true; check which filter_type SelectivityOptionalFilter reports.
issues.expected_gain: q02: a few ms on the supplier branch (the CTE side).
issues.generality: Star joins with a tiny filtered dimension probed by a wider table. The selectivity guard limits the downside.
issues.risk: Low-medium; must not apply to joins that keep NULL or unmatched probe rows.
